summary:
Nia Okoye is scale-keeper who is hard to cheat and easy to ask. The life that shows in public is anchored at Red Clay cistern yard. Nia keeps the cistern yard scales honest and notices who has not had water. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Just, bright, and hard to fool. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: a scar in the work is from a choice they would make again and they will deny it until the second conversation. If that truth surfaces at Red Clay cistern yard, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
